item.title: Samoa island sees sea turtles return after invasive animals are removed, restoring wildlife
item.description: The ecosystem of Nu'utele Island is flourishing thanks to successful conservation strategies that eliminated invasive species. This revitalization has enabled native flora to rebound, supporting local farmers in sustainable crop cultivation. The eradication of predatory species has also facilitated the revival of native birds, while sea turtles have finally returned to lay their eggs on the island’s shores after years of absence.

item.title: Man buys box of old medals for £25, discovers rare Captain Cook medal worth £5,000
item.description: A man who bought a box of 22 old medals for just £25 at a car-boot sale in West Yorkshire discovered that one was a rare 18th-century medal commemorating Captain James Cook's death in 1779. After selling the other medals for £500, he took the rare piece to an auction house, where it later fetched £5,000. The medal was purchased by the Captain Cook Memorial Museum in Whitby for a special exhibition planned for 2028.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Perry Estate Hits Market: Tyler Perry lists $57m Beverly Hills mansion; once home to royal couple
item.description: Tyler Perry has listed his Beverly Hills mansion for $57 million amid plans to relocate to Puerto Rico. The estate, known for hosting Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, spans approximately 24,600 square feet. Featuring eight bedrooms and extensive amenities, it offers privacy within the exclusive Beverly Ridge Estates community. Perry developed the mansion over several years, completing it in 2012 after acquiring the land in 2004.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Historic Houston Mansion Listing: 1911 Cleveland home asks $3.995m; price up about 70% from 2015
item.description: A remarkable mansion steeped in history, previously tied to the Cleveland family, has hit the market for $3.995 million in Houston. Dating back to 1911, this residence artfully blends timeless architectural features with contemporary enhancements. Nestled within Courtlandt Place, a registered historic district known for its notable early 20th-century homes, this property showcases a substantial value increase since its previous sale at $2.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Final Gala Caps Fundraising: Peyton Manning event raises ₹4.2cr; funds back paediatric dialysis unit
item.description: In its concluding year, Peyton Manning's Celebration of Caring Gala in Indianapolis amassed over $4.2 million dedicated to paediatric healthcare. Over its 18-year run, the event has raised nearly $24 million to enhance children's health initiatives. The proceeds will fund a specialized outpatient paediatric dialysis unit, ensuring vital medical care for children. Manning's devotion to the hospital remains steadfast, promising improved healthcare outcomes for Indiana families.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Chris Hemsworth bought a 10-acre Byron Bay estate for A$7 million; now it is a mega-mansion
item.description: In a bold move away from Hollywood's hustle, Chris Hemsworth and Elsa Pataky have turned a coastal property in Byron Bay into a stunning modern mansion. The residence boasts a breathtaking 50-meter infinity pool, a fully equipped gym, and expansive outdoor areas for leisure. Recent upgrades include a tennis court and a dirt-bike track, enhancing the estate's allure.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Texas man excluded from mother's will loses 70-acre property battle after court ruling
item.description: A Texas couple have lost their legal battle to remain on 70 acres of land they say had been in their family for decades. The dispute began after William Dan Moss was excluded from his mother's will. Despite challenging the inheritance decision and subsequent eviction, William and his wife, Brenda, failed to overturn the rulings. On October 22, a Texas appeals court upheld the eviction judgment.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Scientists identify mushroom linked to visions of hundreds of tiny, colourful humans
item.description: The intriguing connection between the mushroom species Lanmaoa asiatica and hallucinations has come to light, particularly among users in China and the Philippines. Individuals describe encounters with small figures, a shared vision across multiple cultures. While the inquiry dates back to 1934, current advancements in identifying mushrooms provide fresh biological insights.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: US court overturns $1.55 million judgment against couple who sought a $150,000 home price cut
item.description: A Michigan appeals court has made headlines by overturning a hefty judgment against a couple who backed out of purchasing a luxury residence. Following an inspection that unveiled critical defects, the couple tried to renegotiate the price but ended up facing a breach of contract lawsuit. The trial court had favored the sellers, but the appeals court clarified the buyers' rights regarding inspection clauses, ultimately nullifying the ruling.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Michigan appeals court orders protection order against Arizona father cancelled in custody dispute
item.description: A father in Arizona has successfully appealed a protection order placed against him by his child's mother. The Michigan Court of Appeals reversed an earlier court decision and ordered the protection order to be canceled. This dispute arose after the mother moved to Michigan with their child, preventing scheduled parenting time. The appeals court found that the mother did not provide sufficient evidence for the protection order.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Halle Berry helps select filmmakers for Tribeca-Chanel program, awarding $120,000 for a short film
item.description: Halle Berry participated in a mentorship panel in New York City, selecting five teams to empower women and non-binary filmmakers through guidance and financial support. Among the winners were Gem Little and Kseniya Yorsh, awarded for their short film, COWARDS. The program not only offered workshops but also ensured ongoing assistance for project completion. Applications will be reopened prior to the 2027 Tribeca Festival.

item.title: Started in 1969 for his children, Jack Klingbeil’s miniature railway grew into a family attraction
item.description: In Wasilla, Alaska, a charming miniature railway stretches 3.5 miles, proudly family-run since 1969. This enchanting railroad features tunnels, bridges, and whimsical scale-model towns, captivating visitors of all ages. As a nonprofit organization, it thrives on volunteer support, offering memorable train rides, including a special chair car for those with special needs. Donations and volunteer efforts are vital for its ongoing maintenance and potential expansions.
